Since Nigeria's output vastly exceeds other African producers like DR Congo and Ghana, being the world's top producer inherently means being Africa's top producer as well.

claim: Joe Biden was the first in his family to go to college.
justification: Biden made this exact claim at the CNN town hall, but he himself admitted in 1987 that it was untrue, telling the New York Times 'there are Finnegans, my mother's family, that went to college.' The claim originated as a plagiarized line from British politician Neil Kinnock, and reporting also indicates Biden's father attended Johns Hopkins University for a year, further contradicting the 'first in family' claim.

claim: COVID-19 was developed as a bioweapon from a research facility in China.
justification: Multiple independent scientific analyses, including genomic studies by virologists (Andersen et al.), found no genetic evidence of engineering and explicitly state there is 'no evidence at all' for the bioweapon theory. This is distinct from the separately debated 'lab leak' hypothesis (accidental release of a natural virus), which the claim does not accurately represent since it specifically asserts deliberate 'development' as a weapon.

claim: 24 of every 100 kids in US schools speak Spanish.
justification: Biden did say this exact phrase on Sept 16, 2020 in Kissimmee, FL, but PolitiFact rated it 'Half True' because the actual nationwide percentage of K-12 students who speak Spanish is about 15-17%, not 24%. Experts believe Biden conflated the percentage of students who are ethnically Hispanic (~26%) with those who actually speak Spanish, which are not the same thing.

claim: Kim Martin Morrow the CEO of Netflix has just been charged with 15 charges for child pornography and 31,000 files have been found on his personal computers for child porn from ages 8 and as young as toddlers.
justification: Multiple independent fact-checks (Heavy/Politifact/Telemundo, ThatsNonsense, Lead Stories, Distractify) confirm 'Kim Martin Morrow' does not exist among Netflix's executives or board members, and no arrest or charges of this kind occurred against Netflix's actual co-CEOs (Reed Hastings/Ted Sarandos). The claim is a debunked hoax that emerged after backlash over the film 'Cuties,' evolving from an earlier fake story about Reed Hastings.

claim: The US government has plans to force a COVID-19 vaccine on everyone.
justification: At the time the claim was made (September 2020), U.S. officials, including Dr. Fauci, publicly and repeatedly stated there was no plan to mandate a COVID-19 vaccine for the general population, saying the federal government would not 'mandate and force anyone to take a vaccine.' No federal plan or policy from that period supports a claim of forcing vaccination on 'everyone'; later 2021 mandates applied only to specific groups (federal workers, contractors, large employers) and were mostly overturned or withdrawn, not a blanket mandate on the entire population.

claim: In India, actor Kangana Ranaut was forced to vote for the Shiv Sena in the elections as they were in alliance with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
justification: Kangana Ranaut did make this claim in a Times Now interview, but independent fact-checkers (India Today's Kamlesh Sutar and The Quint's WebQoof) found it factually incorrect: BJP candidates (Ashish Shelar in the Assembly election, Poonam Mahajan in the Lok Sabha election) were on the ballot in her Bandra West constituency in every relevant election, meaning she was never actually restricted to voting only for Shiv Sena. She deleted her tweets after being confronted with this evidence.

claim: Crime has increased in Minneapolis in 2020.
justification: Multiple independent sources, including contemporaneous Star Tribune reporting from September 2020 and year-end police statistics, confirm violent crime in Minneapolis surged in 2020, up 17% year-to-date by mid-September and ending the year roughly 21% above the five-year average, with record numbers of shooting victims. Property crime also rose modestly. This is corroborated by later academic studies and encyclopedic summaries covering the same period.

claim: A 6 year old boy begged God to save his mother's life after she was ambushed. Today the NFL honored the organization that yelled "hope they die" outside the mothers hospital.
justification: Both underlying facts are true in isolation: protesters did yell 'We hope they die' outside the hospital treating the ambushed deputies, and the NFL did display Black Lives Matter messaging that same week. However, no reporting identifies the small group of hospital protesters as members of Black Lives Matter or any specific 'organization,' so the claim's implication that the NFL honored the same group responsible for the hospital chant is an unsupported conflation of two separate events.

claim: Muslim regiment of the Indian Army had refused to fight in India’s 1965 war with Pakistan.
justification: Multiple retired senior Indian Army officers (Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain, Maj Gen Shashi Asthana) and independent fact-checks (Alt News/The Wire, BBC Hindi, India TV, DFRAC) confirm the Indian Army never had a religiously-designated 'Muslim regiment', so it could not have refused to fight or been disbanded in 1965. Contrary to the claim, Muslim soldiers like Abdul Hamid earned India's highest gallantry award fighting Pakistan in that very war, and 120 armed forces veterans publicly denounced the claim as fake news.

claim: A Rafale Aircraft crashed during training and two pilots are dead.
justification: Contemporary reporting (The Week, Sept 13 2020) identified this exact claim — a Rafale crashing during training near Ambala with two pilots dead — as a hoax spread via fake journalist and fake IAF Twitter handles starting Sept 4, 2020. The photos used as 'evidence' were traced to an unrelated 2019 Mirage 2000 crash in Bengaluru, and no Indian government or air force source confirmed any such Rafale crash in September 2020.

claim: The Indian UPSC examination is discriminatory in favour of Muslim candidates.(Sudarshan News Editor-in-Chief, Suresh Chavhanke, 11 September, 2020, UPSC Jihad Par Ab Tak Ka Sabse Bada Khulasa (The Biggest Expose of All Time on UPSC Jihad)
justification: The Supreme Court explicitly found the show's specific factual claims about Muslims getting a higher age limit and more attempts than Hindus in UPSC to be 'factually incorrect,' and independent fact-checks confirmed age relaxations are based on caste category (SC/ST/OBC), not religion, and that Muslim qualification percentages (3-5%) showed no sudden discriminatory rise. The Information & Broadcasting Ministry also found the show breached the programme code and was likely to promote communal attitudes, and the Court called the broadcast an 'insidious' attempt to vilify the Muslim community rather than a factual exposé.

claim: Former FBI Director James Comey and former CIA Director John Brennan have been charged with multiple counts of treason.
justification: At the time this claim was posted (September 2020), neither Comey nor Brennan faced any criminal charges. Even years later, reporting through 2025-2026 shows Comey was indicted only for allegedly lying to Congress (not treason), and Brennan was under investigation/referral but never actually charged with anything, let alone 'multiple counts of treason.' The word 'treason' appears only in political rhetoric (e.g., Gabbard's 'treasonous conspiracy' memo), not as an actual criminal charge.

claim: Donald Trump tweeted that he was donating $500,000 each toward the expenses of the two Los Angeles County sheriff's deputies who were shot and critically injured on September 12, 2020.
justification: Extensive contemporaneous news coverage documents Trump's actual tweets about the September 12, 2020 shooting of two LA County sheriff's deputies, which called the shooter 'Animals that must be hit hard' and called for the death penalty if the deputies died — no source mentions any $500,000 donation pledge. The attributed handle '@RealDonaldTrwp' is also a misspelling of Trump's real account (@realDonaldTrump), suggesting this may originate from an impersonation account rather than an authentic statement.

claim: The UK public won’t be able to claim compensation if unlicensed vaccines damage our health.
justification: While there was a legitimate concern in September 2020 about compensation for emergency-authorised 'unlicensed' COVID vaccines, the UK government specifically extended the Vaccine Damage Payment Scheme to cover COVID-19 vaccinations (including those under emergency use authorisation) via a Statutory Instrument effective 31 December 2020, before any mass public rollout occurred. Additional legal routes such as product liability and clinical negligence claims also remained available, contradicting the blanket claim that the public would have no compensation route.

claim: Ignat Shchetinin And Sammy Scott Piatt, charged with arson connected to Clackamas County, Oregon wildfires.
justification: Both men were genuinely arrested and charged with arson in Clackamas County in September 2020, but multiple sources (KOIN, Pamplin Media, BuzzFeed News, and Lead Stories fact-check) confirm police explicitly said these incidents were unrelated to the actual wildfires raging in the area — one was a Fred Meyer clothing fire tied to a personal dispute, the other a small leaf pile fire near a building. The claim's phrasing implies a link to the wildfires that authorities specifically debunked.

claim: Edo State in Nigeria has a 19% unemployment rate.
justification: A genuine NBS statistic shows Edo's unemployment rate at 19% for Q2 2019, and this figure was used in Obaseki's campaign messaging around the September 2020 debate period, but independent fact-checkers found that graphics circulating after the debate falsely presented this older 2019 figure as current 2020 data and falsely attributed it to NBS, which the agency denied designing. No direct transcript evidence was found confirming Obaseki spoke the exact '19%' figure on air during the debate itself, and even if used, the figure was outdated by the September 2020 debate given COVID-19's economic impact on employment.

claim: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings was arrested by the FBI after being caught with 13,000 files of child pornography.
justification: Multiple fact-checkers (Snopes, Lead Stories, USA Today via Distractify, IBTimes) confirmed this was a fabricated hoax story published by the fake news site Toronto Today in September 2020 amid backlash over Netflix's film 'Cuties.' Hastings was never arrested or charged, and even Toronto Today itself pulled the article and denied being its original source.

claim: The eligibility criteria for applying to take the exam for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) of India, differentiates depending on whether you are a Hindu or a Muslim.
justification: UPSC's official eligibility rules (age limits, number of attempts, cutoffs) are based on social/administrative categories like SC, ST, OBC, EWS, and disability status — not religion. Independent fact-checks (e.g., The Wire) of nearly identical claims made in the 2020 'UPSC Jihad' controversy confirmed the actual UPSC notification applies age and attempt relaxations by category, not by religion, and that general-category Muslims face the same six-attempt, age-32 rules as general-category Hindus. Data also shows Muslim candidates are underrepresented (3-5%) relative to their population share, contradicting any notion of religious favoritism in eligibility.

claim: Biden called law enforcement the enemy.
justification: Biden did use the word 'enemy' in a July 2020 interview, but only in the narrow context of militarized police using armored vehicles in unfamiliar neighborhoods becoming perceived as 'the enemy' -- not a general condemnation of law enforcement. Independent fact-checks (PolitiFact, CNN, Media Matters) rated similar Trump/Pence claims as taking Biden's words out of context or outright false, since Biden explicitly opposed defunding police and proposed increased community-policing funding.

claim: Muslim candidates are allowed more attempts at the UPCS (i.e. Union Public Service Commission for recruitment to higher Civil Services of the Government of India) exam than others
justification: UPSC's official notifications tie the number of attempts and age relaxation strictly to social/caste categories (General/EWS, OBC, SC/ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen, disability), not to religion. Fact-checks of the specific Sudarshan News 'UPSC Jihad' broadcast confirmed the notification contains no religion-based attempt or age restriction, and that General-category Muslims are limited to the same six attempts as General-category Hindus, while OBC/SC/ST Muslims get the same extra attempts as OBC/SC/ST Hindus.

claim: Police: Political Activists Didn’t Cause Oregon’s Wildfires
justification: Multiple independent, contemporaneous sources (FBI Portland, Ashland Police, Oregon State Police, Douglas County Sheriff, OPB, NPR, NBC News) from September 2020 confirm that law enforcement explicitly debunked rumors that antifa, Proud Boys, or other political activists started Oregon's wildfires. The Ashland Police Chief called the antifa rumor '100% false information' and the FBI stated investigated reports of extremist involvement were found to be untrue.

claim: Nigeria was the third most terrorised in the world in 2020, after Afghanistan and Iraq.
justification: The underlying ranking fact (Nigeria 3rd, behind Afghanistan and Iraq) matches both the 2019 GTI (released Nov 2019) and the later 2019/2020 GTI, so the ordinal claim itself is accurate. However, a dedicated fact-check of this exact TVC broadcast found it misleading because at the time of airing (Sept 10, 2020) the 2020 GTI had not yet been released (it launched in November 2020), and TVC presented the data under a 'GLOBAL TERRORISM INDEX 2020' graphic alongside other inaccurate claims (e.g., that Nigeria ranked worse than Syria, Yemen, and Somalia, which is false since those countries ranked below Nigeria).

claim: Clinical trials of a vaccine against COVID-19 were paused
justification: Multiple independent sources (AP, CBS, Nature, Fortune, French outlets like France Info, France Bleu, Medscape) confirm that AstraZeneca paused global Phase 3 clinical trials of its Oxford-developed COVID-19 vaccine on September 8-9, 2020, after a UK participant experienced a serious adverse reaction. AstraZeneca itself confirmed the pause in an official statement. This matches the claim's date and context precisely.

claim: Western Wildfires Are evidence Of A Coordinated Antifa Campaign To 'Burn The Country Down
justification: The claim that antifa was conducting a 'coordinated campaign' to burn the country down via the 2020 Western wildfires was investigated and explicitly debunked by the FBI's Portland field office and multiple county sheriff's offices in Oregon, which found the specific antifa-arson rumors 'untrue.' Reporting also traced the rumor's spread partly to Russian state media and found no evidence of any organized arson campaign by antifa; Facebook subsequently removed posts spreading this claim.

claim: US Democratic Vice Presidential nominee Kamala Harris tweeted that she ‘filed a complaint’ to remove a specific Instagram account.
justification: No independent reporting, news archive, or fact-check could be found confirming that Kamala Harris tweeted about having 'filed a complaint' to remove a specific Instagram account around September 9, 2020. Searches only surfaced her 2019 letter to Twitter's CEO about Trump's account (a different platform, different context, different year) and unrelated coverage of online abuse targeting her on Instagram/Facebook. The claim appears to originate solely from an Instagram post and cannot be corroborated.

claim: Asha Ranaut tweeted ‘you havent crushed my daughter’s office but Bal Thackeray’s soul.
justification: Independent reporting (India.com, IndiaTV) confirms Asha Ranaut tweeted a message addressed to Uddhav Thackeray on September 9, 2020, stating that the demolition of Kangana's office crushed the soul of late Bal Thackeray rather than the office itself, closely matching the paraphrased claim.
